transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-20
Time: 14:00 - 15:00 PT
Duration: 60 minutes
Attendees: Priya Rao (Redwood AE), Jonah Kim (Redwood SE), Maya Singh (Redwood Partner PM), Liam O'Neill (EmberLink Head of GTM), Sofia Martinez (EmberLink Channel Manager), Daniel Cho (EmberLink Sales Ops)

Auto-generated summary (may be imperfect): weekly pipeline sync, discuss co-sell incentives, confirm technical pilot scope, agree on next steps and deliverables.

[00:00] Priya Rao: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick roll call?
[00:06] Liam O'Neill: Liam here. good to be back.
[00:08] Sofia Martinez: Sofia on my end.
[00:10] Daniel Cho: Daniel. thanks.
[00:12] Priya Rao: Great. Jonah from our SE team, Maya from partner program. Jonah do you want to kick off the tech bits later but for now I'll run high level pipeline?
[00:20] Jonah Kim: yeah, i'll do a quick run then follow with pilot reqs, uh there might be some network nuance with emberlink's customers.
[00:28] Priya Rao: Cool. So quick agenda: pipeline by region, incentives, pilots, and open items. we have the shared deck (link: https://redwood.example.com/decks/partner-cosell-emberlink.pdf) and the spreadsheet with deal names. i put a note on the sheet for a couple of big ones.
[00:44] Sofia Martinez: saw that, thanks. question on the referral credit — is that, like, applied at close or at kick-off?
[00:50] Priya Rao: it's typically applied at close but we can do a partial credit on first invoice for certain enterprise deals - need to check with finance for exceptions. i'll follow up.
[00:58] Liam O'Neill: ok good. high level pipeline: we have 12 partner-sourced opps across NA and EU; 3 in late stage (legal proc), 4 in POC, rest in discovery. biggest by ARR is "Skyline Health" (B2B medtech) and "NimbleDocs" - both referenced in the sheet.
[01:17] Daniel Cho: can you put estimated close dates in the sheet? sales ops needs that for forecasting.
[01:21] Sofia Martinez: yeah will do, but want to confirm Redwood's timeline on POC support - how quickly can you spin up a demo env?
[01:27] Jonah Kim: for hosted API it's pretty quick, like same-day token access for devs; for dedicated or private we usually need 2-4 weeks provisioning depending on capacity and region. just to flag, we had some confusion last time around "Redwood Dedicated" being called 'dedicatedy' in notes, haha.
[01:44] Liam O'Neill: interesting - most of our pipeline prefers a VPC option, customers are sensitive to data residency and audit logs.
[01:50] Priya Rao: understood. for those, we recommend Redwood Private (VPC) — we can run a pilot in a customer VPC or our private deployment depending on the customer's requirement.
[01:58] Jonah Kim: also want to call out perf tradeoffs — quantization and batching can materially change latency vs cost. if the customer needs latency <150ms 95th, we often suggest dedicated GPU pools.
[02:12] Sofia Martinez: a couple customers asked about certs — SOC 2, ISO. do you have up-to-date compliance docs we can share?
[02:18] Maya Singh: yes, i'll drop the compliance pack in the partner folder. it's the same one we share with prospects; i'll include SOC2 and ISO and a redacted audit log example.
[02:26] Priya Rao: i'll add a note: Maya to share compliance pack. (action item)
[02:30] Jonah Kim: on the technical pilot side, i'd like to propose a short benchmark plan: 1) get sample schema and a small dataset (10-50 transcripts or documents), 2) run 3 model variants (open-llama-ish, quantized variant, and a higher quality open model) for latency and cost per token, 3) report back latency p95, token cost, and quality notes.
[02:50] Daniel Cho: when you say open-llama-ish, you mean the community models? sometimes our customers mention "Open Llama" but they really mean the 'open set', transcripts sometimes capture it wrong.
[02:58] Jonah Kim: yes exactly, sorry — i mean the community open models family. our benchmarks will include a small fine-tune or prompt engineering step as needed.
[03:06] Liam O'Neill: timeline for that benchmark?
[03:08] Jonah Kim: if we get sample data by monday (2026-11-23), we can run a first pass by next friday (2026-11-27). depends on access and whether it's hosted or needs dedicated infra.
[03:18] Sofia Martinez: two customers in EU might require data residency; is that supported?
[03:22] Priya Rao: yes, we have EU regions and Private deploy options; we'll flag which of the opps need EU-only and we'll map to our infra.
[03:30] Liam O'Neill: another ask — for co-sell incentives, do you have a standard referral credit % or is it deal-specific?
[03:36] Priya Rao: standard is 10% referral credit at close, but for Strategic deals we can discuss higher or multi-stage credits. i'll send the partner program terms.
[03:44] Daniel Cho: fine. also procurement questions: some of our buyers want a dedicated SLA and longer data retention — how is that handled?
[03:51] Maya Singh: we have add-ons for retention and premium SLA — typical enterprise contracts cover that and pricing varies by retention window and throughput SLAs.
[03:59] Priya Rao: ok moving to specific deals: Liam had flagged "Skyline Health" — can you walk through status?
[04:05] Liam O'Neill: sure. Skyline is in legal review, they want a VPC deployment, security questionnaire almost complete. main blocker is they want a pilot that includes PHI-simulated data in a secured environment.
[04:16] Jonah Kim: for PHI we recommend Private (on-prem or dedicated VPC) + customer KMS. we can support that but need to scope encryption at rest and key management.
[04:24] Sofia Martinez: do you support customer-managed keys?
[04:26] Maya Singh: yes, KMS integrations and HSM support for customers that require it. we'll include a KMS integration note in the compliance pack.
[04:34] Daniel Cho: great. Skyline wants a pilot start in early december, is that feasible?
[04:38] Priya Rao: feasible if we get procurement done and we can finalize SOW; need 2-4 weeks to provision the Private infra. timeline tight but possible.
[04:46] Liam O'Neill: next deal: "NimbleDocs" — they are leaning towards hosted but want lower per-token cost. any suggestions?
[04:54] Jonah Kim: caching/prefix caching and batching can reduce unit cost; Optimize team has recommendations on quantization profiles. for cost-sensitive customers, a quantized variant plus aggressive batching often hits the sweet spot. we'll share Optimize recommendations.
[05:08] Priya Rao: action: Jonah to share a short doc on batching/caching recommendations.
[05:12] Jonah Kim: noted.
[05:14] Sofia Martinez: on the pilot logistics, who owns the SOW and order form? emberlink or redwood?
[05:18] Priya Rao: typically we draft a pilot SOW and emberlink signs as reseller or co-seller depending on arrangement. ops will route through the partner channel.
[05:26] Liam O'Neill: ok. for visibility — can we get weekly joint pipeline export to our CRM? we can map fields.
[05:32] Priya Rao: yes, we can provide a CSV export; i'll coordinate with your ops. share the field mapping.
[05:38] Daniel Cho: we'll share the field mapping by end of day tomorrow.
[05:41] Sofia Martinez: question about competitive positioning — some of our customers evaluate Anthropic and OpenAI; what are the crisp points we want to emphasize from Redwood?
[05:49] Priya Rao: focus on production reliability, cost controls (batching, quant profiles), and unified deployment options — hosted, dedicated, private. also our tooling around rollouts and tracing for regression detection.
[05:59] Jonah Kim: and mention kernel/compilation optimizations for throughput on GPUs; sometimes transcriptions say 'kernel comp action' but it's basically our per-model kernel selection pipeline.
[06:08] Liam O'Neill: good.
[06:10] Priya Rao: okay last section — partner enablement. maya, what does the onboarding look like?
[06:15] Maya Singh: 1) we run a partner kick-off and technical enablement for the AE/SE teams, 2) provide partnership playbook and co-sell deck, 3) share partner portal access and sales resources. typical enablement is 1-2 weeks.
[06:29] Sofia Martinez: can we get a recording of the enablement sessions for our sales team?
[06:32] Maya Singh: yes we'll record and post.
[06:35] Priya Rao: recap and next steps: Priya to send updated co-sell deck + pricing spreadsheet (action); Jonah to share benchmark runbook and batching doc; Maya to drop compliance pack and partner playbook; Liam to give pilot account list and contact emails; schedule exec intro for last week of November.
[06:52] Liam O'Neill: sounds good. any blockers?
[06:54] Daniel Cho: none from ops if we get the field mapping.
[06:57] Priya Rao: cool — we'll follow up in email and update the shared sheet. thanks everyone.
[06:62] [crosstalk] Sofia Martinez: thanks all, bye.

Notes about transcription: occasional mis-heard product names (eg "Open Llama" transcribed variably), timestamps are approximate.
